```{r}
# Load libraries 

# The {"if (require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")"} - for loading and installing packages in a single command -> only need to do this once

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(sf, terra, tidyverse, tidyterra, colorspace, ggrepel, patchwork, tmap, trend, slider, forcats, viridis, viridisLite, scales, hexbin, ggh4x, scico, ggridges, truncnorm, zoo, cowplot, ggplotify, png, magick, ggtext, grid, elevatr, whitebox)

# DATA HANDLING#
# tidyverse -> for data manipulation, cleaning, and visualisation in a cohesive framework
# forcats -> for managing factors (categorical variables)
# slider -> for rolling or sliding window calculations
# zoo -> for working with ordered observations, especially time-series data, with irregular time steps
# elevatr   → for downloading SRTM DEM tiles automatically
# whitebox  → R bindings for WhiteboxTools hydrological processing

# SPATIAL DATA & MAPPING#
# sf -> for handling vector spatial data (points, lines, polygons)
# terra -> for handling and processing raster data
# tidyterra -> for using tidyverse tools on terra objects
# tmap -> for creating thematic maps

# VISUALISATION#
# viridis -> for perceptually uniform color palettes
# viridisLite -> same use as above though I shall use this for R^2 (Temporal Performance raster)
# scales -> for controlling plot scale formatting (e.g., number and date labels)
# hexbin -> for visualizing point density with hexagonal bins
# ggh4x -> for advanced ggplot2 features = facetted_pos_scales
# scico -> for scientific color maps
# colorspace -> for a wide variety of perceptually uniform color palettes
# ggrepel -> for preventing text labels from overlapping
# patchwork -> for combining multiple plots into one figure
# ggridges -> for creating ridge plots (joy plots)
# truncnorm -> for generating random numbers from a truncated normal distribution
# cowplot -> for arranging multiple ggplot objects and converting other plot types into ggplot-compatible objects 
# ggplotify -> for converting non-ggplot objects (like base R plots or tmap grobs) into ggplot objects
# png -> for basic reading and writing of PNG files into raw pixel arrays
# magick -> for professional-grade image processing, editing, and format conversion
# ggtext → enhanced text rendering in ggplot2 using Markdown/HTML (e.g., bold, italics, styled labels)

# STATISTICAL ANALYSIS#
#trend -> for analysing trends in time-series data = Theil-Sen slope
```

```{r}
list(
  Africa = st_crs(Africa.Country.Boundaries)$epsg,
  Kenya = st_crs(Kenya.Admin.Boundary)$epsg,
  PAs = st_crs(Kenya.Terrestrial.PAs)$epsg,
  TsavoWest = st_crs(TsavoWest)$epsg,
  Ngulio = st_crs(NguliaSanctuary)$epsg,
  IPZ = st_crs(TsavoWestIPZ)$epsg
)
```

```{r}
# Adding Attributes to the Ngulia and IPZ
NguliaSanctuary <- NguliaSanctuary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    NAME = "Ngulia Sanctuary",
    ZONE = "Sanctuary"
  )

TsavoWestIPZ <- 
  TsavoWestIPZ |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    NAME = "Intensive Protection Zone",
    ZONE = "IPZ"
  )
```

```{r}
# Merging Ngulia and IPZ into a single sf object (TW.Rhino.Range)
TsavoWest.Rhino.Range <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  NguliaSanctuary,
  TsavoWestIPZ
)
```

```{r}
# Ensuring all CRS match
RPI_CRS <- crs(RPI)
TsavoWest <- st_transform(TsavoWest, RPI_CRS)
TsavoWest.Rhino.Range <- st_transform(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range, RPI_CRS)
```

```{r}
# Visualising RPI for each Area
```

```{r}
## Visualising Tsavo West NP - RPI 
TsavoWest.RPI.Mask <- mask(RPI, TsavoWest)
TsavoWest.RPI.Crop <- crop(TsavoWest.RPI.Mask, TsavoWest)

# Averaging across years for visualisation
TsavoWest.RPI.Mean <- mean(TsavoWest.RPI.Crop, na.rm = TRUE)

# Plotting
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean) +
  
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis"), 
            col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean RPI", reverse = TRUE)) +
  
  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
  
  tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 2) +
  
  tm_title("Spatial Distribution of Mean RPI in Tsavo West NP") +
  
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE) +
  
  tm_view(
  basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap"
  )
)
```

```{r}
# Preliminary Section: Temporal Performance Overview
```

```{r}
## Clipping Temporal Performance to Kenya Admin Boundary

### Ensure CRS matches
Kenya.Admin.Boundary <- st_transform(Kenya.Admin.Boundary, crs(Temporal.Performance))

### Convert to terra vector
Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect <- vect(Kenya.Admin.Boundary)

### Crop and mask
Temporal.Performance.Kenya <- crop(Temporal.Performance, Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect)
Temporal.Performance.Kenya <- mask(Temporal.Performance.Kenya, Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect)
```

```{r}
# Mapping Temporal Performance Metrics (MAE, RMSE, R²) across Kenya

  # names(Temporal.Performance.Kenya) <- c("mae","rmse","rsq")

# 1. MAE
Map.MAE <- tm_shape(Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["mae"]]) +
  tm_raster(
  col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "scico.roma", style = "quantile", n = 7, midpoint = NA),
  col_alpha = 0.8,
  col.legend = tm_legend(title = "MAE")
) +
  tm_shape(Kenya.Admin.Boundary) +
  tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 0.5) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "white",      # Using a dummy color with 0 alpha for transparency
    fill_alpha = 0, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 2, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "orange", 
    fill_alpha = 0.2, 
    col = "darkred", 
    lwd = 1.5, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_title("Mean Absolute Error") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE) +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap")
    )

# 2. RMSE
Map.RMSE <- tm_shape(Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["rmse"]]) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "scico.vik", style = "quantile", n = 7, midpoint = NA),
    col_alpha = 0.8,
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "RMSE")
  ) +
  tm_shape(Kenya.Admin.Boundary) +
  tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 0.5) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "white",      # Using a dummy color with 0 alpha for transparency
    fill_alpha = 0, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 2, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "orange", 
    fill_alpha = 0.2, 
    col = "darkred", 
    lwd = 1.5, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_title("Root Mean Squared Error") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE) +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap")
    )

# 3. R²
Map.Rsqd <- tm_shape(Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["rsq"]]) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "scico.bam", style = "quantile", n = 7, midpoint = NA),
    col_alpha = 0.8,
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = expression(R^2))
  ) +
  tm_shape(Kenya.Admin.Boundary) +
  tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 0.5) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "white",      # Using a dummy color with 0 alpha for transparency
    fill_alpha = 0, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 2, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "orange", 
    fill_alpha = 0.2, 
    col = "darkred", 
    lwd = 1.5, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_title(expression(R^2)) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE) +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap")
    )

# Arrange side by side
tmap_arrange(Map.MAE, Map.RMSE, Map.Rsqd, ncol = 3)
```

```{r}
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap"))

# 3. Es (Soil Evaporation)
PMLv2.ES.Map <- tm_shape(PMLv2.Kenya[["Es"]]) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "viridis", style = "quantile", n = 7),
    col_alpha = 0.8,

    fill_alpha = 0, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 2, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "orange", 
    fill_alpha = 0.2, 
    col = "darkred", 
    lwd = 1.5, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_title("Soil Evaporation") +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap"))

# 4. Ei (Interception)
PMLv2.EI.Map <- tm_shape(PMLv2.Kenya[["Ei"]]) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "viridis", style = "quantile", n = 7),
    col_alpha = 0.8,
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Ei (Interception)")
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "white",      # Using a dummy color with 0 alpha for transparency
    fill_alpha = 0, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 2, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_shape(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "orange", 
    fill_alpha = 0.2, 
    col = "darkred", 
    lwd = 1.5, 
    id = "NAME"
  ) +
  tm_title("Interception") +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c(
    "Esri.WorldImagery",
    "OpenStreetMap",
    "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    "Esri.WorldTopoMap"))

# Arrange in a 2x2 panel
tmap_arrange(PMLv2.GPP.Map, PMLv2.EC.Map, PMLv2.ES.Map, PMLv2.EI.Map, ncol = 2)
```

```{r}
# SECTION 1: Zone-Level RPI Summaries
# Extracting pixel values per zone into data frames
# for statistical comparison
```

```{r}
# Name RPI layers by Hydrological Year
# 22 hydrological years: Sep 2000–Aug 2001 to Sep 2021–Aug 2022

n_years <- nlyr(RPI)

Hydro.Year.Labels <- paste0(
  2000:(2000 + n_years - 1), "-",
  substr(2001:(2001 + n_years - 1), 3, 4)
)
# e.g. "2000-01", "2001-02", ..., "2021-22"

names(RPI) <- Hydro.Year.Labels
```

```{r}
# Create "Tsavo West excl. Rhino Range" zone
# This is the KEY comparison zone for the habitat gap analysis:
# the broader park habitat that rhinos could potentially expand into

TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange <- st_difference(
  TsavoWest,
  st_union(TsavoWest.Rhino.Range)  |> st_transform(st_crs(TsavoWest))
)
```

```{r}
# Reusable extraction function
# Extracts all pixel values from the RPI stack for a given zone
# Returns a long-format tibble (one row per pixel per year)

extract_rpi_pixels <- function(raster_stack, boundary_sf, zone_name, year_labels) {
  
  boundary_vect <- vect(boundary_sf)
  
  terra::extract(raster_stack, boundary_vect, xy = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(ZONE = zone_name) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = all_of(year_labels),
      names_to  = "Hydro.Year",
      values_to = "RPI"
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(RPI)) |>
    mutate(
      Year.Start = as.integer(substr(Hydro.Year, 1, 4)),  # numeric year for trend fitting
      ZONE = factor(ZONE)
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Extract pixel values for all zones

cat("Extracting RPI pixels — Tsavo West NP...\n")
RPI.Pixels.TsavoWest <- extract_rpi_pixels(
  RPI, TsavoWest, "Tsavo West NP", Hydro.Year.Labels
)

cat("Extracting RPI pixels — Ngulia Sanctuary...\n")
RPI.Pixels.Ngulia <- extract_rpi_pixels(
  RPI, NguliaSanctuary, "Ngulia Sanctuary", Hydro.Year.Labels
)

cat("Extracting RPI pixels — Intensive Protection Zone...\n")
RPI.Pixels.IPZ <- extract_rpi_pixels(
  RPI, TsavoWestIPZ, "Intensive Protection Zone", Hydro.Year.Labels
)

cat("Extracting RPI pixels — Tsavo West Rhino Range (combined)...\n")
RPI.Pixels.RhinoRange <- extract_rpi_pixels(
  RPI, TsavoWest.Rhino.Range, "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)", Hydro.Year.Labels
)

cat("Extracting RPI pixels — Tsavo West excl. Rhino Range...\n")
RPI.Pixels.TW.Excl <- extract_rpi_pixels(
  RPI, TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange, "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)", Hydro.Year.Labels
)
```

```{r}
# Combine all zones into one master pixel-level data frame

RPI.All.Zones.Pixels <- bind_rows(
  RPI.Pixels.TsavoWest,
  RPI.Pixels.Ngulia,
  RPI.Pixels.IPZ,
  RPI.Pixels.RhinoRange,
  RPI.Pixels.TW.Excl
) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(
      ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    )
  )

cat("Master pixel data frame dimensions:", dim(RPI.All.Zones.Pixels), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Annual summary table (Zone × Year)
# Used for time-series plots and trend analysis

RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary <- RPI.All.Zones.Pixels |>
  group_by(ZONE, Hydro.Year, Year.Start) |>
  summarise(
    Mean.RPI    = mean(RPI,                    na.rm = TRUE),
    Median.RPI  = median(RPI,                  na.rm = TRUE),
    SD.RPI      = sd(RPI,                      na.rm = TRUE),
    Q10.RPI     = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.10,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q25.RPI     = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.25,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q75.RPI     = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.75,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q90.RPI     = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.90,  na.rm = TRUE),
    N.Pixels    = n(),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Overall summary table (Zone × all years combined)
# Used for the static habitat gap comparison

RPI.Zone.Overall.Summary <- RPI.All.Zones.Pixels |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  summarise(
    Mean.RPI        = mean(RPI,                    na.rm = TRUE),
    Median.RPI      = median(RPI,                  na.rm = TRUE),
    SD.RPI          = sd(RPI,                      na.rm = TRUE),
    Q10.RPI         = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.10,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q25.RPI         = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.25,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q75.RPI         = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.75,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q90.RPI         = quantile(RPI, probs = 0.90,  na.rm = TRUE),
    N.Pixels.Total  = n(),
    .groups         = "drop"
  )

# Quick print to verify
print(RPI.Zone.Overall.Summary)
```

```{r}
# SECTION EXTENSION: PMLv2 & StudyPixels Zone Extractions
# Building a unified habitat profile per zone combining:
# → Productivity (RPI)
# → Water-energy fluxes (PMLv2)
# → Land cover composition (StudyPixels)
```

```{r}
# Confirm band names before extracting

cat("PMLv2 band names:     ", names(PMLv2.Kenya), "\n")
cat("StudyPixels band names:", names(StudyPixelsKenya), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Align CRS of PMLv2 and StudyPixels to RPI CRS
# (already done for vector layers; doing same for rasters)

PMLv2.Kenya       <- project(PMLv2.Kenya,       crs(RPI))
StudyPixelsKenya  <- project(StudyPixelsKenya,   crs(RPI), method = "near")
# Note: method = "near" for StudyPixels because IGBP is categorical
# (nearest-neighbour preserves class integer values)
```

```{r}
# Clip PMLv2 and StudyPixels to Tsavo West NP extent
# Reduces memory and focuses on the study area

TsavoWest.Vect <- vect(TsavoWest)

PMLv2.TsavoWest      <- crop(PMLv2.Kenya,      TsavoWest.Vect) |>
                         mask(TsavoWest.Vect)

StudyPixels.TsavoWest <- crop(StudyPixelsKenya, TsavoWest.Vect) |>
                          mask(TsavoWest.Vect)
```

```{r}
# Reusable extraction function for continuous multi-band rasters (PMLv2 fluxes + cover bands)
# Returns a long-format tibble: one row per pixel per band

extract_multiband_pixels <- function(raster_stack, boundary_sf, zone_name) {
  
  boundary_vect <- vect(boundary_sf)
  band_names    <- names(raster_stack)
  
  terra::extract(raster_stack, boundary_vect, xy = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(ZONE = zone_name) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = all_of(band_names),
      names_to  = "Band",
      values_to = "Value"
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(Value)) |>
    mutate(ZONE = factor(ZONE))
}
```

```{r}
# Extract PMLv2 pixel values per zone
# (GPP, Ec, Es, Ei — all continuous)

cat("Extracting PMLv2 pixels — Tsavo West NP...\n")
PMLv2.Pixels.TsavoWest <- extract_multiband_pixels(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest, TsavoWest, "Tsavo West NP"
)

cat("Extracting PMLv2 pixels — Ngulia Sanctuary...\n")
PMLv2.Pixels.Ngulia <- extract_multiband_pixels(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest, NguliaSanctuary, "Ngulia Sanctuary"
)

cat("Extracting PMLv2 pixels — Intensive Protection Zone...\n")
PMLv2.Pixels.IPZ <- extract_multiband_pixels(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest, TsavoWestIPZ, "Intensive Protection Zone"
)

cat("Extracting PMLv2 pixels — Rhino Range (combined)...\n")
PMLv2.Pixels.RhinoRange <- extract_multiband_pixels(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest, TsavoWest.Rhino.Range, "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)"
)

cat("Extracting PMLv2 pixels — Tsavo West excl. Rhino Range...\n")
PMLv2.Pixels.TW.Excl <- extract_multiband_pixels(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest, TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange, "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)"
)

# Combine all PMLv2 zone pixels
PMLv2.All.Zones.Pixels <- bind_rows(
  PMLv2.Pixels.TsavoWest,
  PMLv2.Pixels.Ngulia,
  PMLv2.Pixels.IPZ,
  PMLv2.Pixels.RhinoRange,
  PMLv2.Pixels.TW.Excl
) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(
      ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    ),
    # Clarify band labels for plotting later
    Band = fct_recode(Band,
      "GPP (gC/m²/yr)"           = "GPP",
      "Canopy Transpiration (mm)" = "Ec",
      "Soil Evaporation (mm)"     = "Es",
      "Interception (mm)"         = "Ei"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Extract StudyPixels — continuous cover bands only
#   (trees, shrubland, grassland, bare, allRangelands)
# IGBP handled separately below (Next section) as it is categorical

StudyPixels.Continuous <- StudyPixels.TsavoWest[[
  c("trees", "shrubland", "grassland", "bare", "allRangelands")
]]

cat("Extracting StudyPixels (continuous) — Tsavo West NP...\n")
```

```{r}
# Extract StudyPixels — IGBP categorical band
# Summarised as class frequency (%) per zone rather than
# pixel-level values, since it is a nominal variable

extract_igbp_freq <- function(raster_stack, boundary_sf, zone_name) {
  
  boundary_vect <- vect(boundary_sf)
  
  terra::extract(raster_stack[["igbp"]], boundary_vect) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    rename(IGBP_Class = igbp) |>
    filter(!is.na(IGBP_Class)) |>
    count(IGBP_Class) |>
    mutate(
      ZONE        = zone_name,
      Pct_Pixels  = n / sum(n) * 100,
      # Decode IGBP integer codes to labels
      IGBP_Label  = case_when(
        IGBP_Class == 6  ~ "Closed Shrubland",
        IGBP_Class == 7  ~ "Open Shrubland",
        IGBP_Class == 8  ~ "Woody Savanna",
        IGBP_Class == 9  ~ "Savanna",
        IGBP_Class == 10 ~ "Grassland",
        TRUE             ~ paste0("Class ", IGBP_Class)
      )
    )
}

IGBP.TsavoWest  <- extract_igbp_freq(StudyPixels.TsavoWest, TsavoWest,                  "Tsavo West NP")
IGBP.Ngulia     <- extract_igbp_freq(StudyPixels.TsavoWest, NguliaSanctuary,             "Ngulia Sanctuary")
IGBP.IPZ        <- extract_igbp_freq(StudyPixels.TsavoWest, TsavoWestIPZ,                "Intensive Protection Zone")
IGBP.RhinoRange <- extract_igbp_freq(StudyPixels.TsavoWest, TsavoWest.Rhino.Range,       "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)")
IGBP.TW.Excl    <- extract_igbp_freq(StudyPixels.TsavoWest, TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange,   "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)")

IGBP.All.Zones <- bind_rows(
  IGBP.TsavoWest,
  IGBP.Ngulia,
  IGBP.IPZ,
  IGBP.RhinoRange,
  IGBP.TW.Excl
) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(
      ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Build the Unified Zone Profile Table
# One row per zone — combines RPI + PMLv2 + land cover means
# This is the master comparison table for the habitat gap analysis

# 15a. PMLv2 summary per zone (wide format)
PMLv2.Zone.Summary <- PMLv2.All.Zones.Pixels |>
  group_by(ZONE, Band) |>
  summarise(Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Band, values_from = Mean) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0("Mean.", gsub("[^A-Za-z]", ".", .x)),
              .cols = -ZONE)

# 15b. Cover summary per zone (wide format)
Cover.Zone.Summary <- Cover.All.Zones.Pixels |>
  group_by(ZONE, Band) |>
  summarise(Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Band, values_from = Mean) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0("Mean.", gsub("[^A-Za-z]", ".", .x)),
              .cols = -ZONE)

# 15c. Dominant IGBP class per zone
IGBP.Dominant <- IGBP.All.Zones |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  slice_max(Pct_Pixels, n = 1) |>
  select(ZONE, Dominant.IGBP = IGBP_Label, Dominant.IGBP.Pct = Pct_Pixels) |>
  ungroup()

# 15d. Join everything into the unified profile table
Unified.Zone.Profile <- RPI.Zone.Overall.Summary |>
  left_join(PMLv2.Zone.Summary,  by = "ZONE") |>
  left_join(Cover.Zone.Summary,  by = "ZONE") |>
  left_join(IGBP.Dominant,       by = "ZONE")

# Print the unified profile
print(Unified.Zone.Profile)
```

```{r}
# SECTION 2: Temporal Trend Analysis
# Theil-Sen slopes across the 22-year RPI time series (2000–2023)
# Answering: has the RPI gap between the Rhino Range and the
# rest of Tsavo West been growing, shrinking, or stable?
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Add 5-year rolling mean to the annual summary table
  # Uses slider::slide_dbl() — centred window, .before=2, .after=2
  # Smooths interannual rainfall-driven variability so the
  # underlying productivity trend is easier to interpret

RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary <- RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  arrange(Year.Start) |>
  mutate(
    Rolling.Mean.5yr = slide_dbl(
      Mean.RPI,
      mean,
      .before   = 2,
      .after    = 2,
      .complete = FALSE   # retain edge years with partial windows
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# Quick check
RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary |>
  select(ZONE, Hydro.Year, Mean.RPI, Rolling.Mean.5yr) |>
  print(n = 10)
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Zone-level Theil-Sen slopes
  # Applied to each zone's 22-year annual mean RPI time series
  # trend::sens.slope() performs both:
  #   → Sen's slope (median of all pairwise slopes) = magnitude
  #   → Mann-Kendall test = statistical significance

RPI.Zone.Trends <- RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  arrange(Year.Start) |>
  summarise(
    Sen.Slope       = as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(Mean.RPI)$estimates),
    P.Value         = trend::sens.slope(Mean.RPI)$p.value,
    CI.Lower        = trend::sens.slope(Mean.RPI)$conf.int[1],
    CI.Upper        = trend::sens.slope(Mean.RPI)$conf.int[2],
    MK.Z.Statistic  = as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(Mean.RPI)$statistic),
    N.Years         = n(),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Significance = case_when(
      P.Value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      P.Value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      P.Value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      P.Value < 0.10  ~ ".",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    Trend.Direction = case_when(
      P.Value < 0.05 & Sen.Slope > 0 ~ "Significant Increase",
      P.Value < 0.05 & Sen.Slope < 0 ~ "Significant Decrease",
      TRUE                           ~ "No Significant Trend"
    ),
    # Express slope as RPI change per decade for interpretability
    Sen.Slope.Per.Decade = Sen.Slope * 10
  )

print(RPI.Zone.Trends)
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Pixel-level Theil-Sen slope raster
  # Applied to each pixel's 22-year RPI time series independently
  # Produces a 2-band raster:
  #   Band 1 → Sen's slope (trend magnitude per year)
  #   Band 2 → Mann-Kendall p-value (statistical significance)

# Helper function — applied to each pixel's time series vector
compute_pixel_sens_slope <- function(x) {
  # Require at least 8 non-NA years for a reliable trend estimate
  if (sum(!is.na(x)) < 8) return(c(Sen.Slope = NA_real_, P.Value = NA_real_))
  result <- trend::sens.slope(x[!is.na(x)])
  c(
    Sen.Slope = as.numeric(result$estimates),
    P.Value   = as.numeric(result$p.value)
  )
}

cat("Computing pixel-level Theil-Sen slopes across Tsavo West NP...\n")
cat("(This may take a few minutes given raster extent)\n")

RPI.Trend.Raster <- app(
  TsavoWest.RPI.Crop,
  fun   = compute_pixel_sens_slope,
  cores = 2   # adjust to your machine; use parallel::detectCores() - 1 for max
)

names(RPI.Trend.Raster) <- c("Sen.Slope", "P.Value")

# Create a significance mask — pixels with p < 0.05 only
RPI.Trend.Significant <- RPI.Trend.Raster[["Sen.Slope"]]
RPI.Trend.Significant[RPI.Trend.Raster[["P.Value"]] >= 0.05] <- NA

# Quick summary of trend raster
cat("\nPixel-level trend summary (all pixels):\n")
global(RPI.Trend.Raster, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\nPixel-level trend summary (significant pixels only, p < 0.05):\n")
global(RPI.Trend.Significant, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Step 4: RPI gap trajectory analysis
  # The core expansion feasibility question:
    # Is the productivity advantage of the Rhino Range over the rest of Tsavo West growing, shrinking, or stable over time?

RPI.Gap.Annual <- RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary |>
  filter(ZONE %in% c(
    "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
    "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)"
  )) |>
  select(ZONE, Hydro.Year, Year.Start, Mean.RPI, Rolling.Mean.5yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = ZONE,
    values_from = c(Mean.RPI, Rolling.Mean.5yr)
  ) |>
  rename(
    RhinoRange.Mean.RPI     = `Mean.RPI_Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)`,
    TW.Excl.Mean.RPI        = `Mean.RPI_Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)`,
    RhinoRange.Rolling.5yr  = `Rolling.Mean.5yr_Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)`,
    TW.Excl.Rolling.5yr     = `Rolling.Mean.5yr_Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    RPI.Gap         = RhinoRange.Mean.RPI    - TW.Excl.Mean.RPI,
    RPI.Gap.Rolling = RhinoRange.Rolling.5yr - TW.Excl.Rolling.5yr
  ) |>
  arrange(Year.Start)

# Theil-Sen trend on the gap itself
Gap.Trend.Result <- trend::sens.slope(RPI.Gap.Annual$RPI.Gap)

RPI.Gap.Trend.Summary <- tibble(
  Metric              = "RPI Gap (Rhino Range minus TW excl.)",
  Sen.Slope           = as.numeric(Gap.Trend.Result$estimates),
  Sen.Slope.Per.Decade = as.numeric(Gap.Trend.Result$estimates) * 10,
  P.Value             = Gap.Trend.Result$p.value,
  CI.Lower            = Gap.Trend.Result$conf.int[1],
  CI.Upper            = Gap.Trend.Result$conf.int[2],
  MK.Z.Statistic      = as.numeric(Gap.Trend.Result$statistic),
  Significance        = case_when(
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.10  ~ ".",
    TRUE                             ~ "ns"
  ),
  Interpretation      = case_when(
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.05 & Gap.Trend.Result$estimates > 0 ~
      "Gap is widening — Rhino Range gaining productivity advantage",
    Gap.Trend.Result$p.value < 0.05 & Gap.Trend.Result$estimates < 0 ~
      "Gap is narrowing — Expansion zone converging with Rhino Range",
    TRUE ~
      "Gap is stable — no significant change over 2000-2023"
  )
)

cat("\n--- RPI Gap Trend Summary ---\n")
print(RPI.Gap.Trend.Summary)

cat("\n--- Annual RPI Gap Values ---\n")
print(RPI.Gap.Annual |> select(Hydro.Year, RPI.Gap, RPI.Gap.Rolling))
```

```{r}
# Step 5: Pixel-level trend breakdown by zone
  # Summarise what % of pixels in each zone show significant positive, significant negative, or no trend

# Extract Sen.Slope and P.Value per pixel per zone
extract_trend_pixels <- function(trend_raster, boundary_sf, zone_name) {
  terra::extract(trend_raster, vect(boundary_sf), xy = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    filter(!is.na(Sen.Slope), !is.na(P.Value)) |>
    mutate(
      ZONE = zone_name,
      Trend.Category = case_when(
        P.Value < 0.05 & Sen.Slope > 0 ~ "Significant Increase",
        P.Value < 0.05 & Sen.Slope < 0 ~ "Significant Decrease",
        TRUE                           ~ "No Significant Trend"
      )
    )
}

Trend.Pixels.TsavoWest  <- extract_trend_pixels(RPI.Trend.Raster, TsavoWest,                "Tsavo West NP")
Trend.Pixels.Ngulia     <- extract_trend_pixels(RPI.Trend.Raster, NguliaSanctuary,           "Ngulia Sanctuary")
Trend.Pixels.IPZ        <- extract_trend_pixels(RPI.Trend.Raster, TsavoWestIPZ,              "Intensive Protection Zone")
Trend.Pixels.RhinoRange <- extract_trend_pixels(RPI.Trend.Raster, TsavoWest.Rhino.Range,     "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)")
Trend.Pixels.TW.Excl    <- extract_trend_pixels(RPI.Trend.Raster, TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange, "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)")

# Combine and summarise
RPI.Pixel.Trend.Summary <- bind_rows(
  Trend.Pixels.TsavoWest,
  Trend.Pixels.Ngulia,
  Trend.Pixels.IPZ,
  Trend.Pixels.RhinoRange,
  Trend.Pixels.TW.Excl
) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(
      ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(ZONE, Trend.Category) |>
  summarise(N.Pixels = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  mutate(Pct.Pixels = N.Pixels / sum(N.Pixels) * 100) |>
  ungroup()

cat("\n--- Pixel-level Trend Breakdown by Zone ---\n")
print(RPI.Pixel.Trend.Summary)
```

```{r}
# Map 2.3: Trend Category map (3-class categorical)
  # Significant Increase / Significant Decrease / No Trend
    ## Most visually accessible for a dissertation figure

# Vectorized classification — safe and memory-efficient
RPI.Trend.Category <- RPI.Trend.Raster[["Sen.Slope"]]  # Copy structure of Sen.Slope band
values(RPI.Trend.Category) <- 0L                        # Integer 0 = No Significant Trend

# Assign categories using vectorized logical indexing
RPI.Trend.Category[
  RPI.Trend.Raster[["P.Value"]] < 0.05 & 
  RPI.Trend.Raster[["Sen.Slope"]] > 0
] <- 1L    # Significant Increase

RPI.Trend.Category[
  RPI.Trend.Raster[["P.Value"]] < 0.05 & 
  RPI.Trend.Raster[["Sen.Slope"]] < 0
] <- -1L   # Significant Decrease

# Preserve original NAs
RPI.Trend.Category[is.na(RPI.Trend.Raster[["Sen.Slope"]])] <- NA

# Name the layer
names(RPI.Trend.Category) <- "Trend.Category"

# Free RAM before plotting
gc()

# Static plotting to avoid risk of R crashing
tmap_mode("plot")

        "Significant Increase"
      )
    ),
    col_alpha   = 0.85,
    col.legend  = tm_legend(title = "RPI Trend\n(2000–2023)")

  tm_shape(TsavoWest) +
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 3.1: RPI Distribution Comparison -> This is the single most powerful static comparison figure.

  # Violin + Box plot — full pixel-level distributions per zone
    # Draws from "RPI.All.Zones.Pixels":
      # Shows the full pixel-level RPI distribution per zone — the violin gives the shape, the box gives Q25/median/Q75, and individual outlier points are suppressed given the pixel count. 

# Subsample pixels for plotting efficiency
# (717,000 × 5 zones is too many points for smooth rendering)
set.seed(42)
RPI.Plot.Sample <- RPI.All.Zones.Pixels |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5000) |>
  ungroup()

Fig3.1.RPI.Distribution.Comparison <- ggplot(
  RPI.Plot.Sample,
  aes(x = ZONE, y = RPI, fill = ZONE, colour = ZONE)
) +

  # Violin — full distribution shape
  geom_violin(
    alpha      = 0.35,
    linewidth  = 0.4,
    trim       = TRUE,
    scale      = "width"
  ) +

  # Boxplot inside violin — Q25, median, Q75
  geom_boxplot(
    width         = 0.15,
    alpha         = 0.7,
    linewidth     = 0.5,
    outlier.shape = NA     # suppress outlier dots given pixel count
  ) +

  # Median point
  stat_summary(
    fun      = median,
    geom     = "point",
    shape    = 21,
    size     = 2.5,
    fill     = "white",
    colour   = "black",
    stroke   = 0.8
  ) +

  # Reference line at RPI = 1 (actual GPP = potential GPP)
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey40",
    linewidth  = 0.5
  ) +

  annotate(
    "text",
    x     = 5.4,
    y     = 1.02,
    label = "RPI = 1\n(Actual = Potential)",
    size  = 2.8,
    colour = "grey40",
    hjust  = 1
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = Zone.Colours)   +
  scale_colour_manual(values = Zone.Colours) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 14)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1.5),
    breaks = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.25)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Relative Productivity Index Distribution by Zone",
    subtitle = "Tsavo West National Park — Hydrological Years 2000–2023",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Relative Productivity Index (RPI)",
    caption  = "Each violin shows the full pixel-level RPI distribution (n = 5,000 pixels sampled per zone).\nBoxplot shows Q25, median, Q75. White point = median. Dashed line = RPI of 1 (actual GPP = potential GPP)."
  ) +

  theme_rpi() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")   # x-axis labels are sufficient

Fig3.1.RPI.Distribution.Comparison
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 3.2: Annual RPI Time Series with Rolling Mean
  # Focused on the three key comparison zones

    # Draws from "RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary": 
      # One line per zone across 2000–2023, with a shaded Q25–Q75 ribbon for uncertainty and the 5-year rolling mean overlaid as a bolder line. Focuses on the three key zones: Tsavo West NP, Tsavo West excl. Rhino Range, and Rhino Range combined.

# Filter to the three key zones for clarity
Key.Zones <- c(
  "Tsavo West NP",
  "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
  "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)"
)

RPI.TimeSeries.Data <- RPI.Zone.Annual.Summary |>
  filter(ZONE %in% Key.Zones) |>
  mutate(ZONE = fct_relevel(ZONE, Key.Zones))

Fig3.2.RPI.TimeSeries.RollingMean <- ggplot(
  RPI.TimeSeries.Data,
  aes(x = Year.Start, colour = ZONE, fill = ZONE)
) +

  # Uncertainty ribbon — Q25 to Q75
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Q25.RPI, ymax = Q75.RPI),
    alpha     = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Annual mean — thin line
  geom_line(
    aes(y = Mean.RPI, linetype = ZONE),
    linewidth = 0.55,
    alpha     = 0.65
  ) +

  # 5-year rolling mean — bold line
  geom_line(
    aes(y = Rolling.Mean.5yr, linetype = ZONE),
    linewidth = 1.1,
    alpha     = 1
  ) +

  # Mark the rolling mean with a subtle point at each year
  geom_point(
    aes(y = Rolling.Mean.5yr),
    size  = 1.5,
    shape = 21,
    fill  = "white",
    stroke = 0.6
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = Zone.Colours[Key.Zones])   +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = Zone.Colours[Key.Zones])   +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = Zone.Linetypes[Key.Zones]) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, 2022, by = 2),
    labels = paste0(seq(2000, 2022, by = 2), "\n–",
                    substr(seq(2001, 2023, by = 2), 3, 4))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0.45, 0.95),
    breaks = seq(0.45, 0.95, by = 0.10)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Annual Mean RPI Trajectory by Zone (2000–2023)",
    subtitle = "Thin line = annual mean | Bold line = 5-year rolling mean | Ribbon = interquartile range (Q25–Q75)",
    x        = "Hydrological Year",
    y        = "Mean Relative Productivity Index (RPI)",
    colour   = "Zone",
    fill     = "Zone",
    linetype = "Zone",
    caption  = "RPI = Actual GPP / Potential GPP. Potential GPP estimated via quantile regression forest (Lomax et al.2025).\nHydrological year runs September–August."
  ) +

  theme_rpi() +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  )

Fig3.2.RPI.TimeSeries.RollingMean
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 3.3: RPI Gap Trajectory (Rhino Range vs TW excl.)

    # Draws from "RPI.Gap.Annual": 
      # A single panel showing the annual gap and its 5-year rolling mean, with a horizontal reference line at zero and an annotated stable trend finding from Section 2.

Fig3.3.Gap.Trajectory <- ggplot(
  RPI.Gap.Annual,
  aes(x = Year.Start)
) +

  # Zero reference line — gap = 0 means zones are equal
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey40",
    linewidth  = 0.6
  ) +

  # Shade positive gap (Rhino Range > TW excl.) in green
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = 0, ymax = pmax(RPI.Gap, 0)),
    fill  = "#1b7837",
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # Shade negative gap (rare years where TW excl. > Rhino Range) in orange
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pmin(RPI.Gap, 0), ymax = 0),
    fill  = "#d95f02",
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # Annual raw gap
  geom_line(
    aes(y = RPI.Gap),
    colour    = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.55,
    linetype  = "solid"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(y = RPI.Gap),
    colour = "grey50",
    size   = 1.8,
    shape  = 21,
    fill   = "white"
  ) +

  # 5-year rolling gap — bold
  geom_line(
    aes(y = RPI.Gap.Rolling),
    colour    = "#1b7837",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # Trend annotation from Section 2 results
  annotate(
    "text",
    x      = 2001,
    y      = 0.21,
    label  = "Gap is stable (Sen's slope = +0.000440/yr, p = 1.00, ns)",
    size   = 3.0,
    colour = "grey30",
    hjust  = 0,
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, 2022, by = 2),
    labels = paste0(seq(2000, 2022, by = 2), "\n–",
                    substr(seq(2001, 2023, by = 2), 3, 4))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-0.05, 0.25, by = 0.05),
    labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "RPI Productivity Gap: Rhino Range vs. Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
    subtitle = "Grey line = annual gap | Green bold line = 5-year rolling mean | Green shading = Rhino Range more productive",
    x        = "Hydrological Year",
    y        = "RPI Gap (Rhino Range − Tsavo West excl.)",
    caption  = "Positive values indicate the Rhino Range is more productive than the potential expansion zone.\nTheil-Sen slope applied to annual gap series. Shaded band below zero indicates years where gap briefly reverses."
  ) +

  theme_rpi()
```

```{r}
# SECTION 4(A): Land Cover × RPI Cross-Analysis
  # Linking PMLv2/StudyPixels to RPI for habitat characterisation
    # Answering: WHY does the productivity gap exist?
      # Point-sampling all variables at RPI pixel locations
        # Eliminates coordinate mismatch from different raster grids
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Get unique RPI pixel centroids as a SpatVector
  # These become the master sampling locations for everything

RPI.Centroids <- RPI.Pixel.Mean |>
  distinct(x, y)

RPI.Centroids.Vect <- vect(
  RPI.Centroids,
  geom = c("x", "y"),
  crs  = crs(RPI)
)

cat("Total unique RPI pixel locations:", nrow(RPI.Centroids), "\n")

# Quick sanity check — confirm points fall within Tsavo West
cat("Points within Tsavo West extent: should be TRUE\n")
print(relate(ext(RPI.Centroids.Vect), ext(vect(TsavoWest)), "intersects"))
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Sample Cover raster AT RPI pixel locations
  # terra::extract() for SpatVector points returns one row
    # per point in the same order as input — safe to bind x,y back
      # Note: raster stores 0-1 proportions → multiply by 100

cat("Sampling Cover raster at RPI pixel locations...\n")

Cover.Sampled <- terra::extract(
  StudyPixels.Continuous,     # 5-band raster: trees, shrubland, grassland, bare, allRangelands
  RPI.Centroids.Vect
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    x = RPI.Centroids$x,
    y = RPI.Centroids$y
  ) |>
  rename(
    Tree.Pct      = trees,
    Shrubland.Pct = shrubland,
    Grassland.Pct = grassland,
    Bare.Pct      = bare,
    Rangeland.Pct = allRangelands
  ) |>
  # Raster stores 0-1 proportions — convert to %
  mutate(across(
    c(Tree.Pct, Shrubland.Pct, Grassland.Pct, Bare.Pct, Rangeland.Pct),
    ~ . * 100
  )) |>
  select(-ID)

cat("Cover sampled — dimensions:", dim(Cover.Sampled), "\n")
cat("Cover value range check (Shrubland %):",
    round(range(Cover.Sampled$Shrubland.Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Sample PMLv2 raster AT RPI pixel locations

cat("Sampling PMLv2 raster at RPI pixel locations...\n")

PMLv2.Sampled <- terra::extract(
  PMLv2.TsavoWest,     # 4-band raster: GPP, Ec, Es, Ei
  RPI.Centroids.Vect
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    x = RPI.Centroids$x,
    y = RPI.Centroids$y
  ) |>
  rename(
    GPP.Annual = GPP,
    Ec.Annual  = Ec,
    Es.Annual  = Es,
    Ei.Annual  = Ei
  ) |>
  select(-ID)

cat("PMLv2 sampled — dimensions:", dim(PMLv2.Sampled), "\n")
cat("GPP value range check (gC/m²/yr):",
    round(range(PMLv2.Sampled$GPP.Annual, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 4: Sample IGBP raster AT RPI pixel locations
  # Handles Fig 4.4 directly — no separate join step needed

cat("Sampling IGBP raster at RPI pixel locations...\n")

IGBP.Sampled <- terra::extract(
  StudyPixels.TsavoWest[["igbp"]],
  RPI.Centroids.Vect
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    x = RPI.Centroids$x,
    y = RPI.Centroids$y,
    IGBP.Label = case_when(
      igbp == 6  ~ "Closed\nShrubland",
      igbp == 7  ~ "Open\nShrubland",
      igbp == 8  ~ "Woody\nSavanna",
      igbp == 9  ~ "Savanna",
      igbp == 10 ~ "Grassland",
      TRUE       ~ paste0("Class ", igbp)
    )
  ) |>
  select(-ID, -igbp)

cat("IGBP sampled — dimensions:", dim(IGBP.Sampled), "\n")
cat("IGBP classes found:", unique(IGBP.Sampled$IGBP.Label), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 5: Build master cross-analysis table
  # All joins now use x, y from the same RPI centroid grid
    # No coordinate mismatch possible

Pixel.CrossAnalysis <- RPI.Pixel.Mean |>
  left_join(Cover.Sampled,  by = c("x", "y")) |>
  left_join(PMLv2.Sampled,  by = c("x", "y")) |>
  left_join(IGBP.Sampled,   by = c("x", "y")) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Shrubland.Pct),
    !is.na(GPP.Annual)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    )
  )

cat("Master cross-analysis table dimensions:", dim(Pixel.CrossAnalysis), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 6: Verification — must show real numbers, not NA

Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  summarise(
    N.Pixels    = n(),
    Mean.RPI    = round(mean(Mean.RPI,      na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Mean.Shrub  = round(mean(Shrubland.Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Mean.Grass  = round(mean(Grassland.Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Mean.GPP    = round(mean(GPP.Annual,    na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    IGBP.Classes = n_distinct(IGBP.Label, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  print()
```

```{r}
# Step 7: Build Pixel.IGBP.RPI for Fig 4.4
  # Directly from Pixel.CrossAnalysis
Pixel.IGBP.RPI <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  filter(
    !is.na(IGBP.Label),
    ZONE %in% c(
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)"
    )
  )

cat("IGBP × RPI table:\n")
Pixel.IGBP.RPI |>
  group_by(ZONE, IGBP.Label) |>
  summarise(
    N        = n(),
    Mean.RPI = round(mean(Mean.RPI, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  print()
```

```{r}
# Step 7 (Revised): Add shrubland intensity bins to Pixel.CrossAnalysis
  # Replaces IGBP class comparison with ESA shrubland intensity


Pixel.CrossAnalysis <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  mutate(
    Shrub.Class = case_when(
      Shrubland.Pct < 25              ~ "Low Shrub\n(<25%)",
      Shrubland.Pct >= 25 &
        Shrubland.Pct < 50            ~ "Moderate Shrub\n(25–50%)",
      Shrubland.Pct >= 50 &
        Shrubland.Pct < 75            ~ "High Shrub\n(50–75%)",
      Shrubland.Pct >= 75             ~ "Very High Shrub\n(≥75%)",
      TRUE                            ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Shrub.Class = fct_relevel(
      Shrub.Class,
      "Low Shrub\n(<25%)",
      "Moderate Shrub\n(25–50%)",
      "High Shrub\n(50–75%)",
      "Very High Shrub\n(≥75%)"
    )
  )

# Rebuild the Fig 4.4 data object using shrubland bins
Pixel.Shrub.RPI <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Shrub.Class),
    ZONE %in% c(
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)"
    )
  )

# Verify bin counts per zone — confirms distribution is meaningful
cat("Shrubland intensity bin counts per zone:\n")
Pixel.Shrub.RPI |>
  group_by(ZONE, Shrub.Class) |>
  summarise(
    N        = n(),
    Mean.RPI = round(mean(Mean.RPI, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  print()

# Rebuild subsample to include the new Shrub.Class column
set.seed(42)
Pixel.CrossAnalysis.Sample <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  slice_sample(n = 3000) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 4.1: Mean RPI × Shrubland Cover (%)
  # The primary mechanistic relationship — shrubland as the
    # driver of productivity advantage in the Rhino Range

Fig4.1.RPI.Shrub <- ggplot(
  Pixel.CrossAnalysis.Sample |>
    filter(ZONE %in% c(
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Tsavo West NP"
    )),
  aes(x = Shrubland.Pct, y = Mean.RPI)
) +

  # Hexbin density layer
  geom_hex(
    aes(fill = after_stat(count)),
    bins      = 35,
    colour    = NA
  ) +

  scale_fill_scico(
    palette = "lajolla",
    name    = "Pixel\ncount",
    trans   = "log10"
  ) +

  # Smoothed trend line per facet
  geom_smooth(
    method    = "loess",
    se        = TRUE,
    colour    = "#1b7837",
    fill      = "#1b7837",
    alpha     = 0.15,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  # Reference line at RPI = 1
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey50",
    linewidth  = 0.5
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ ZONE,
    ncol   = 3,
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%")
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1.6),
    breaks = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.25)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Relationship Between Shrubland Cover and Habitat Productivity (RPI)",
    subtitle = "Each hexagon represents pixel density. Green line = LOESS smoother with 95% CI.",
    x        = "Shrubland Cover (%)",
    y        = "Mean RPI (2000–2023)",
    caption  = "Mean RPI averaged across 22 hydrological years per pixel. Shrubland cover from ESA WorldCover resampled to 500m."
  ) +

  theme_rpi()
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 4.3: Spearman Correlation Heatmap
  # All cover + flux variables × all zones

# Compute Spearman correlations per zone
Spearman.Correlations <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  summarise(
    r.Shrubland  = cor(Mean.RPI, Shrubland.Pct, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Grassland  = cor(Mean.RPI, Grassland.Pct, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Tree       = cor(Mean.RPI, Tree.Pct,       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Bare       = cor(Mean.RPI, Bare.Pct,       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.GPP        = cor(Mean.RPI, GPP.Annual,     method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Ec         = cor(Mean.RPI, Ec.Annual,       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Es         = cor(Mean.RPI, Es.Annual,       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = starts_with("r."),
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Spearman.r"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Variable = fct_recode(Variable,
      "Shrubland (%)"          = "r.Shrubland",
      "Grassland (%)"          = "r.Grassland",
      "Tree Cover (%)"         = "r.Tree",
      "Bare Ground (%)"        = "r.Bare",
      "GPP (gC/m²/yr)"        = "r.GPP",
      "Canopy Transpiration"   = "r.Ec",
      "Soil Evaporation"       = "r.Es"
    ),
    # Logical variable ordering
    Variable = fct_relevel(
      Variable,
      "GPP (gC/m²/yr)", "Canopy Transpiration", "Soil Evaporation",
      "Shrubland (%)", "Grassland (%)", "Tree Cover (%)", "Bare Ground (%)"
    )
  )

Fig4.3.Correlation.Heatmap <- ggplot(
  Spearman.Correlations,
  aes(x = Variable, y = ZONE, fill = Spearman.r)
) +

  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Correlation value labels
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label  = round(Spearman.r, 2),
      colour = abs(Spearman.r) > 0.4   # white text on dark tiles
    ),
    size     = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "grey20"),
    guide  = "none"
  ) +

  scale_fill_scico(
    palette  = "vik",
    limits   = c(-1, 1),
    midpoint = 0,
    name     = "Spearman\ncorrelation (r)"
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 12)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Spearman Correlations: Mean RPI vs. Land Cover & Flux Variables",
    subtitle = "Positive r = variable positively associated with higher RPI | Negative r = associated with lower RPI",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = NULL,
    caption  = "Spearman rank correlation computed at pixel level per zone (full pixel population, not subsampled)."
  ) +

  theme_rpi() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size  = 9),
    panel.grid      = element_blank()
  )

Fig4.3.Correlation.Heatmap
```

```{r}
# FIGURE 4.4 (REVISED): RPI Distribution by Shrubland
  # Intensity Class Across Zones
    # Replaces IGBP single-class plot with ecologically meaningful
      # shrubland cover gradient × zone comparison

# Colour palette for shrubland intensity classes
# Low → pale yellow, Very High → dark green
Shrub.Class.Colours <- c(
  "Low Shrub\n(<25%)"        = "#f7fcb9",
  "Moderate Shrub\n(25–50%)" = "#addd8e",
  "High Shrub\n(50–75%)"     = "#41ab5d",
  "Very High Shrub\n(≥75%)"  = "#006d2c"
)

Fig4.4.Shrub.Profiles <- ggplot(
  Pixel.Shrub.RPI,
  aes(x = Shrub.Class, y = Mean.RPI, fill = Shrub.Class)
) +

  geom_violin(
    alpha     = 0.4,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    trim      = TRUE,
    scale     = "width"   # all violins same width regardless of N
  ) +

  geom_boxplot(
    width         = 0.2,
    alpha         = 0.8,
    linewidth     = 0.45,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +

  stat_summary(
    fun      = median,
    geom     = "point",
    shape    = 21,
    size     = 2.2,
    fill     = "white",
    colour   = "black",
    stroke   = 0.7
  ) +

  # Reference line at RPI = 1
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    colour     = "grey50",
    linewidth  = 0.5
  ) +

  # Annotate pixel counts per bin per zone
  stat_summary(
    aes(label = after_stat(paste0("n=", scales::comma(y)))),
    fun       = function(x) quantile(x, 0.95),
    geom      = "text",
    size      = 2.4,
    colour    = "grey40",
    vjust     = -0.3,
    fun.args  = list()
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ ZONE, ncol = 3) +

    limits = c(0, 1.6),

  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 14)
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Mean RPI by Shrubland Cover Intensity Class Across Zones",
    subtitle = "Violin + boxplot shows pixel-level RPI distribution within each shrubland intensity class per zone.\nWhite point = median. Dashed line = RPI of 1 (actual GPP = potential GPP).",
    x        = "Shrubland Cover Intensity Class (ESA WorldCover)",
    y        = "Mean RPI (2000–2023)",
    caption  = paste0(
      "Shrubland cover (%) from ESA WorldCover 2020 resampled to 500m. ",
      "Bins defined by ecologically meaningful shrub cover thresholds.\n",
      "MODIS IGBP classification not used here due to coarse savanna-grassland ",
      "class conflation at 500m resolution."
    )
  ) +

  theme_rpi() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```

```{r}
# SECTION 4B: Terrain & Hydrology Analysis
  # Integrating topographic and hydrological variables into Tsavo West Rhino Expansion habitat intelligence framework
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Download SRTM DEM for Tsavo West
  # Using elevatr — automatically tiles and mosaics SRTM data
    # z = 10 → ~76m resolution, appropriate for Tsavo West's 9,065 km²
      # z = 11 → ~38m, usable but memory-intensive for this extent

DEM.File.Path <- "C:/Workspace/Mureithi_RPI_TsavoWest_Rhino_Expansion/data/Terrain/TsavoWest_DEM.tif"

if (!file.exists(DEM.File.Path)) {
  
  cat("Downloading SRTM DEM for Tsavo West NP...\n")
  
  # Create the directory if it doesn't exist yet
  dir.create(
    dirname(DEM.File.Path),
    showWarnings = FALSE,
    recursive    = TRUE   # creates all intermediate folders in one go
  )
  
  # Reproject TsavoWest to WGS84 for elevatr (requires lat/lon)
  TsavoWest.WGS84 <- st_transform(TsavoWest, 4326)
  
  TsavoWest.DEM.Raw <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(
    locations = TsavoWest.WGS84,
    z         = 10,
    clip      = "locations"
  )
  
  # Convert raster → terra SpatRaster
  TsavoWest.Elevation <- rast(TsavoWest.DEM.Raw)
  names(TsavoWest.Elevation) <- "Elevation_m"
  
  # Save to disk — avoids re-downloading
  writeRaster(
    TsavoWest.Elevation,
    DEM.File.Path,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
  cat("DEM downloaded and saved.\n")
  
} else {
  cat("DEM already exists — loading from disk.\n")
  TsavoWest.Elevation <- rast(DEM.File.Path)
}

# Reproject DEM to match RPI CRS
TsavoWest.Elevation <- project(TsavoWest.Elevation, crs(RPI))

# Confirm metadata
print(TsavoWest.Elevation)
cat("Elevation range (m):", global(TsavoWest.Elevation, "range", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Compute Terrain Derivatives
  # Elevation → Slope, Aspect, TPI, TRI
    # TRI = Terrain Ruggedness Index — measures mean absolute difference between a cell and its 8 neighbours
      # Directly relevant to large mammal movement cost

cat("Computing terrain derivatives...\n")

TsavoWest.Slope  <- terrain(TsavoWest.Elevation, v = "slope",  unit = "degrees")
TsavoWest.Aspect <- terrain(TsavoWest.Elevation, v = "aspect", unit = "degrees")
TsavoWest.TPI    <- terrain(TsavoWest.Elevation, v = "TPI")
TsavoWest.TRI    <- terrain(TsavoWest.Elevation, v = "TRI")
# TRI: 0 = perfectly flat, higher values = more rugged
# Black rhinos avoid areas with TRI > ~50m (very rugged escarpments)

# Stack all terrain derivatives into one object
TsavoWest.Terrain.Stack <- c(
  TsavoWest.Elevation,
  TsavoWest.Slope,
  TsavoWest.Aspect,
  TsavoWest.TPI,
  TsavoWest.TRI
)
names(TsavoWest.Terrain.Stack) <- c(
  "Elevation_m", "Slope_deg", "Aspect_deg", "TPI", "TRI"
)

# Quick summary of terrain
cat("\nTerrain summary for Tsavo West NP:\n")
global(TsavoWest.Terrain.Stack, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Aspect Reclassification
  # Convert continuous 0–360° into 8 cardinal/intercardinal
    # directions relevant to solar exposure and moisture dynamics
      # North/East aspects: cooler, moister → better browse quality
        # South/West aspects: hotter, drier  → more drought stress

TsavoWest.Aspect.Class <- classify(
  TsavoWest.Aspect,
  rcl = matrix(c(
      0,  22.5, 1,   # North
     22.5, 67.5, 2,  # Northeast
     67.5,112.5, 3,  # East
    112.5,157.5, 4,  # Southeast
    157.5,202.5, 5,  # South
    202.5,247.5, 6,  # Southwest
    247.5,292.5, 7,  # West
    292.5,337.5, 8,  # Northwest
    337.5,360,   1   # North (wraps)
  ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)
names(TsavoWest.Aspect.Class) <- "Aspect_Class"
```

```{r}
# Step 4: Hydrological Processing via WhiteboxTools
  # Full pipeline: DEM → breach → fill → SCA → TWI + streams
    # Save each step to disk — prevents needing to rerun

# Define working directory for WhiteboxTools files
WBT.Dir <- "C:/Workspace/Mureithi_RPI_TsavoWest_Rhino_Expansion/data/Terrain/WBT"
dir.create(WBT.Dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Export DEM to WBT directory (WhiteboxTools works with file paths)
DEM.WBT.Path       <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_DEM_WBT.tif")
DEM.Breached.Path  <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_DEM_Breached.tif")
DEM.Filled.Path    <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_DEM_Filled.tif")
SCA.Path           <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_SCA.tif")
Slope.WBT.Path     <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_Slope_WBT.tif")
TWI.Path           <- file.path(WBT.Dir, "TsavoWest_TWI.tif")

# Export DEM if not already saved for WBT
if (!file.exists(DEM.WBT.Path)) {
  writeRaster(TsavoWest.Elevation, DEM.WBT.Path, overwrite = TRUE)
}

# Step 4a: Breach depressions — carves flow paths through ridges
if (!file.exists(DEM.Breached.Path)) {
  cat("Breaching depressions...\n")
  wbt_breach_depressions(
    dem    = DEM.WBT.Path,
    output = DEM.Breached.Path
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Step 4b: Fill remaining depressions with flat increment
if (!file.exists(DEM.Filled.Path)) {
  cat("Filling depressions...\n")
  wbt_fill_depressions(
    dem            = DEM.Breached.Path,
    output         = DEM.Filled.Path,
    flat_increment = 0.001
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Step 4c: Specific Catchment Area (SCA) — D8 flow accumulation
  # SCA is required as input to TWI: TWI = ln(SCA / tan(slope))
if (!file.exists(SCA.Path)) {
  cat("Computing Specific Catchment Area...\n")
  wbt_d8_flow_accumulation(
    input  = DEM.Filled.Path,
    output = SCA.Path,
    pntr   = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Step 4d: Slope in WhiteboxTools (must match SCA alignment exactly)
if (!file.exists(Slope.WBT.Path)) {
  cat("Computing WBT slope...\n")
  wbt_slope(
    dem    = DEM.Filled.Path,
    output = Slope.WBT.Path
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Step 4e: Topographic Wetness Index
if (!file.exists(TWI.Path)) {
  cat("Computing TWI...\n")
  wbt_wetness_index(
    sca    = SCA.Path,
    slope  = Slope.WBT.Path,
    output = TWI.Path
  )
}

cat("All WhiteboxTools outputs complete.\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 5: Load hydrological outputs back into R
  # Clean TWI, extract streams, compute distance to water

TsavoWest.SCA <- rast(SCA.Path)  |> mask(TsavoWest.Vect)
TsavoWest.TWI <- rast(TWI.Path)  |> mask(TsavoWest.Vect)

# Clean negative TWI values (artefacts from flat areas)
TsavoWest.TWI[TsavoWest.TWI < 0] <- 0

# Reproject to RPI CRS
TsavoWest.SCA <- project(TsavoWest.SCA, crs(RPI))
TsavoWest.TWI <- project(TsavoWest.TWI, crs(RPI))

names(TsavoWest.TWI) <- "TWI"
names(TsavoWest.SCA) <- "SCA"
```

```{r}
# Step 6: Stream Extraction
  # At ~76m resolution: 76 × 76 = 5,776 m² per pixel
    # Threshold of 500 pixels = ~289 ha contributing area
      # Captures meaningful seasonal drainage lines (luggas) relevant to rhino water access

# Reload SCA in its native CRS (before reprojection)
TsavoWest.SCA.Native <- rast(SCA.Path)

# Check what CRS the WBT output is in
cat("Native SCA CRS:\n")
print(crs(TsavoWest.SCA.Native, describe = TRUE))

# Mask to Tsavo West — reproject the vector to match native CRS
TsavoWest.Native.CRS  <- st_transform(TsavoWest, crs(TsavoWest.SCA.Native))
TsavoWest.Native.Vect <- vect(TsavoWest.Native.CRS)

TsavoWest.SCA.Native <- mask(TsavoWest.SCA.Native, TsavoWest.Native.Vect)

# Check SCA value range before thresholding
cat("SCA value range (native):\n")
print(minmax(TsavoWest.SCA.Native))

# Extract streams using native CRS
Stream.Threshold <- 500

TsavoWest.Streams.Native <- TsavoWest.SCA.Native > Stream.Threshold
TsavoWest.Streams.Native[TsavoWest.Streams.Native == 0L] <- NA
TsavoWest.Streams.Native <- mask(TsavoWest.Streams.Native, TsavoWest.Native.Vect)
names(TsavoWest.Streams.Native) <- "Stream"

cat("Stream pixels (native CRS):",
    global(TsavoWest.Streams.Native, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 7: Distance to Water
  # The single most important habitat requirement for black rhinos that RPI does not capture — rhinos need water every 2–4 days
    # Computed as distance from each pixel to nearest stream pixel

# Compute gridDist in native CRS — distance in metres (native units)
cat("Computing distance to nearest water source (native CRS)...\n")

TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native <- terra::gridDist(
  TsavoWest.Streams.Native,
  target = 1
)

# Check range before converting
cat("Raw distance range (native units):\n")
print(minmax(TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native))

# Convert to km
TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native <- TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native / 1000
names(TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native) <- "Dist_to_Water_km"

# NOW reproject to RPI CRS — safe because distance is continuous
TsavoWest.DistToWater <- project(
  TsavoWest.DistToWater.Native,
  crs(RPI),
  method = "bilinear"
)

# Reproject streams for mapping
TsavoWest.Streams <- project(
  TsavoWest.Streams.Native,
  crs(RPI),
  method = "near"    # nearest neighbour preserves binary values
)
TsavoWest.Streams <- mask(TsavoWest.Streams, TsavoWest.Vect)

# Final mask and name
TsavoWest.DistToWater <- mask(TsavoWest.DistToWater, TsavoWest.Vect)
names(TsavoWest.DistToWater) <- "Dist_to_Water_km"

# Confirm range — expect 0 to ~15–25 km for Tsavo West
cat("Distance to water range (km):",
    minmax(TsavoWest.DistToWater)[1], "to",
    minmax(TsavoWest.DistToWater)[2], "\n")
```

```{r}
# Step 8: Extract terrain + hydrology per zone
  # Extend the existing Pixel.CrossAnalysis table with Elevation, Slope, TRI, TWI, Distance to Water

# Stack the variables we want to extract per zone
Terrain.Hydro.Stack <- c(
  TsavoWest.Elevation,
  TsavoWest.Slope,
  TsavoWest.TRI,
  TsavoWest.TWI,
  TsavoWest.DistToWater
)
names(Terrain.Hydro.Stack) <- c(
  "Elevation_m", "Slope_deg", "TRI", "TWI", "Dist_to_Water_km"
)

# Reuse extract_multiband_pixels function from earlier
cat("Extracting terrain + hydrology — Tsavo West NP...\n")
Terrain.Pixels.TsavoWest  <- extract_multiband_pixels(Terrain.Hydro.Stack, TsavoWest,                "Tsavo West NP")

cat("Extracting terrain + hydrology — Ngulia Sanctuary...\n")
Terrain.Pixels.Ngulia     <- extract_multiband_pixels(Terrain.Hydro.Stack, NguliaSanctuary,           "Ngulia Sanctuary")

cat("Extracting terrain + hydrology — Intensive Protection Zone...\n")
Terrain.Pixels.IPZ        <- extract_multiband_pixels(Terrain.Hydro.Stack, TsavoWestIPZ,              "Intensive Protection Zone")

cat("Extracting terrain + hydrology — Rhino Range (combined)...\n")
Terrain.Pixels.RhinoRange <- extract_multiband_pixels(Terrain.Hydro.Stack, TsavoWest.Rhino.Range,     "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)")

cat("Extracting terrain + hydrology — Tsavo West excl. Rhino Range...\n")
Terrain.Pixels.TW.Excl    <- extract_multiband_pixels(Terrain.Hydro.Stack, TsavoWest.Excl.RhinoRange, "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)")

# Combine and pivot to wide format
Terrain.Pixel.Wide <- bind_rows(
  Terrain.Pixels.TsavoWest,
  Terrain.Pixels.Ngulia,
  Terrain.Pixels.IPZ,
  Terrain.Pixels.RhinoRange,
  Terrain.Pixels.TW.Excl
) |>
  mutate(
    ZONE = fct_relevel(ZONE,
      "Tsavo West NP",
      "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
      "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)",
      "Ngulia Sanctuary",
      "Intensive Protection Zone"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(ZONE, x, y),
    names_from  = Band,
    values_from = Value,
    values_fn   = mean        
  ) |>
  mutate(x = round(x, 6), y = round(y, 6))

# Verify columns are now atomic numeric — not lists
cat("Terrain column classes:\n")
sapply(Terrain.Pixel.Wide |> select(-ZONE, -x, -y), class)

# Join to master cross-analysis table
Pixel.CrossAnalysis <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  mutate(x = round(x, 6), y = round(y, 6)) |>
  left_join(Terrain.Pixel.Wide, by = c("ZONE", "x", "y"))

cat("Extended cross-analysis table dimensions:", dim(Pixel.CrossAnalysis), "\n")

# Zone-level terrain + hydrology summary
Terrain.Zone.Summary <- Terrain.Pixel.Wide |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  summarise(
    Mean.Elevation    = mean(Elevation_m,       na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean.Slope        = mean(Slope_deg,          na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean.TRI          = mean(TRI,                na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean.TWI          = mean(TWI,                na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean.Dist.Water   = mean(Dist_to_Water_km,   na.rm = TRUE),
    Median.Dist.Water = median(Dist_to_Water_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    Pct.Within.2km    = mean(Dist_to_Water_km < 2, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups           = "drop"
  )

cat("\n--- Terrain & Hydrology Zone Summary ---\n")
print(Terrain.Zone.Summary)
```

```{r}
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE) +
  tm_view(basemap.server = c("Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap",
                              "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", "Esri.WorldTopoMap"))
```

```{r}
# Subsample for plotting
set.seed(42)
Pixel.Terrain.Sample <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>

  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# Figure B1: Terrain profiles per zone (violin + box)
  # Four panels: Elevation, Slope, TRI, Distance to Water
Terrain.Long <- Pixel.Terrain.Sample |>
  filter(ZONE %in% c(
    "Tsavo West NP",
    "Tsavo West (excl. Rhino Range)",
    "Rhino Range (Ngulia + IPZ)"
  )) |>
  select(ZONE, Elevation_m, Slope_deg, TRI, Dist_to_Water_km) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(Elevation_m, Slope_deg, TRI, Dist_to_Water_km),
    names_to  = "Terrain.Var",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Terrain.Var = fct_recode(Terrain.Var,
      "Elevation (m)"           = "Elevation_m",
      "Slope (°)"               = "Slope_deg",
      "Terrain Ruggedness (TRI)"= "TRI",
      "Distance to Water (km)"  = "Dist_to_Water_km"
    ),
    Terrain.Var = fct_relevel(Terrain.Var,
      "Elevation (m)", "Slope (°)",
      "Terrain Ruggedness (TRI)", "Distance to Water (km)"
    )
  )

FigB1.Terrain.Profiles <- ggplot(
  Terrain.Long,
  aes(x = ZONE, y = Value, fill = ZONE, colour = ZONE)
) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4, trim = TRUE, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.45, outlier.shape = NA) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point",
               shape = 21, size = 2, fill = "white",
               colour = "black", stroke = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = Zone.Colours) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = Zone.Colours) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 12)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Terrain.Var, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title    = "Terrain & Hydrology Profiles by Zone — Tsavo West NP",
    subtitle = "Violin + boxplot shows full pixel-level distribution per zone",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Value",
    caption  = "SRTM DEM at ~76m resolution. Distance to water derived from D8 flow accumulation (threshold = 289 ha)."
  ) +
  theme_rpi() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

FigB1.Terrain.Profiles
```

```{r}
# Figure B4: Extended Spearman correlation heatmap
# Now including terrain + hydrology variables
Spearman.Extended <- Pixel.CrossAnalysis |>
  filter(!is.na(Elevation_m), !is.na(Dist_to_Water_km)) |>
  group_by(ZONE) |>
  summarise(
    r.Shrubland    = cor(Mean.RPI, Shrubland.Pct,    method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Grassland    = cor(Mean.RPI, Grassland.Pct,    method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.GPP          = cor(Mean.RPI, GPP.Annual,        method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Ec           = cor(Mean.RPI, Ec.Annual,         method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Elevation    = cor(Mean.RPI, Elevation_m,       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.Slope        = cor(Mean.RPI, Slope_deg,         method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.TRI          = cor(Mean.RPI, TRI,               method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.TWI          = cor(Mean.RPI, TWI,               method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    r.DistWater    = cor(Mean.RPI, Dist_to_Water_km,  method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = starts_with("r."),
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Spearman.r"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Variable = fct_recode(Variable,
      "Shrubland (%)"          = "r.Shrubland",
      "Grassland (%)"          = "r.Grassland",
      "GPP (gC/m²/yr)"        = "r.GPP",
      "Canopy Transpiration"   = "r.Ec",
      "Elevation (m)"          = "r.Elevation",
      "Slope (°)"              = "r.Slope",
      "Ruggedness (TRI)"       = "r.TRI",
      "Wetness (TWI)"          = "r.TWI",
      "Dist. to Water (km)"    = "r.DistWater"
    ),
    # Group variables by type for visual separation
    Variable.Group = case_when(
      Variable %in% c("GPP (gC/m²/yr)", "Canopy Transpiration")     ~ "Flux",
      Variable %in% c("Shrubland (%)", "Grassland (%)")              ~ "Land Cover",
      TRUE                                                            ~ "Terrain & Hydrology"
    ),
    Variable = fct_relevel(Variable,
      "GPP (gC/m²/yr)", "Canopy Transpiration",
      "Shrubland (%)", "Grassland (%)",
      "Elevation (m)", "Slope (°)", "Ruggedness (TRI)",
      "Wetness (TWI)", "Dist. to Water (km)"
    )
  )

FigB4.Extended.Heatmap <- ggplot(
  Spearman.Extended,
  aes(x = Variable, y = ZONE, fill = Spearman.r)
) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label  = round(Spearman.r, 2),
      colour = abs(Spearman.r) > 0.35
    ),
    size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "grey20"),
    guide  = "none"
  ) +
  scale_fill_scico(
    palette  = "vik",
    limits   = c(-1, 1),
    midpoint = 0,
    name     = "Spearman\ncorrelation (r)"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 12)
  ) +
  # Visual separator between variable groups
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(2.5, 4.5), colour = "grey60",
             linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5,  y = 5.6, label = "Fluxes",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 3.5,  y = 5.6, label = "Land Cover",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 7,    y = 5.6, label = "Terrain & Hydrology",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  labs(
    title    = "Spearman Correlations: Mean RPI vs. Habitat Variables (Extended)",
    subtitle = "Positive r = positively associated with productivity | Negative r = inversely associated",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = NULL,
    caption  = "Spearman rank correlation at pixel level per zone. Variables grouped by type (dashed lines)."
  ) +
  theme_rpi() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid  = element_blank()
  )

FigB4.Extended.Heatmap
```
